questions.question: What do Spaniards often call Valentine's Day, besides "San Valentín"?
questions.fact: Spanish tip: "enamorado" comes from "amor", and "estar enamorado de alguien" means "to be in love with someone".

questions.question: Which hormone is often nicknamed the "love hormone" or "cuddle hormone"?
questions.fact: Oxytocin is released during hugs and touch, and it also plays a big role in childbirth, helping the womb contract during labour.

questions.question: Which British royal couple married at Westminster Abbey in April 2011?
questions.fact: Kate's sister Pippa was maid of honour, and the couple were made Duke and Duchess of Cambridge on the morning of the wedding.

questions.question: Queen Victoria made which wedding dress colour fashionable when she married in 1840?
questions.fact: Before then many brides simply wore their best dress in any colour. Victoria's white satin and lace for her wedding to Prince Albert set the trend.

questions.question: In which Italian city is "Romeo and Juliet" set?
questions.fact: Volunteers known as "Juliet's secretaries" in Verona answer thousands of letters that people write to Juliet every year.

questions.question: In Roman myth, which winged god makes people fall in love by shooting them with arrows?
questions.fact: In Ovid's tale of Apollo and Daphne, Cupid's gold-tipped arrows cause love, while his lead-tipped arrows make people run from it.

questions.question: Which band released "All You Need Is Love" in 1967?
questions.fact: The song was first performed live on "Our World", the first global satellite TV broadcast, watched by hundreds of millions of people.

questions.question: Who had a 1961 hit with "Can't Help Falling in Love"?
questions.fact: Its melody is based on "Plaisir d'amour", a French love song from the 1780s. Elvis often used it to close his concerts.

questions.question: The romantic comedy "Love Actually" is set mainly in which city?
questions.fact: Its opening shows real people greeting loved ones at Heathrow arrivals, reportedly filmed with hidden cameras.

questions.question: Which actor plays dance teacher Johnny Castle in "Dirty Dancing" (1987)?
questions.fact: The film's song "(I've Had) The Time of My Life" won the Oscar for Best Original Song.

questions.question: Which Disney film features the song "Can You Feel the Love Tonight"?
questions.fact: The song was written by Elton John with lyrics by Tim Rice, and it won the Oscar for Best Original Song.

questions.question: Which Hollywood couple was nicknamed "Brangelina"?
questions.fact: They met while filming "Mr. & Mrs. Smith" (2005), in which they played a married couple of secret assassins.

questions.question: Which Hollywood star married Prince Rainier III and became Princess of Monaco?
questions.fact: She gave up acting at 26 when she married in 1956. Alfred Hitchcock reportedly tried to lure her back for his film "Marnie".

questions.question: "Something old, something new, something borrowed, something…" what?
questions.fact: The full Victorian rhyme ends "and a silver sixpence in her shoe", which was meant to bring the couple wealth.

questions.question: Which colour does a bride traditionally wear for luck at a Chinese wedding?
questions.fact: White is traditionally linked with mourning in China, though many modern brides also change into a white Western-style gown.

questions.question: In Spain, which phrase do couples most often use to say "I love you"?
questions.fact: "Te amo" exists too, but in Spain it sounds more intense or poetic. "Te quiero" also works for family and close friends.

questions.question: In Spain, what does calling your partner your "media naranja" mean?
questions.fact: It literally means "half orange". The idea of lovers as two halves looking for each other goes back to Plato's "Symposium".

questions.question: "Ich liebe dich" means "I love you" in which language?
questions.fact: In Dutch it's "Ik hou van jou", and in Swedish it's "Jag älskar dig".

questions.question: Which flower is the classic Valentine's Day gift?
questions.fact: Many of the roses sold in Europe for Valentine's Day are grown in Kenya and Ethiopia and flown in through Dutch flower auctions.

questions.question: In "XOXO" at the end of a message, what does the X stand for?
questions.fact: One popular theory: in the Middle Ages people who couldn't write signed with an X and sometimes kissed it as a sign of good faith.

questions.question: Couples traditionally kiss under which plant at Christmas?
questions.fact: Mistletoe is a partial parasite: it grows on trees such as apple and poplar and takes water and nutrients from its host.

questions.question: Which footballer was Shakira's partner for about 12 years?
questions.fact: They met on the set of the "Waka Waka" video for the 2010 World Cup, which Spain went on to win. They split in 2022.

questions.question: Which Spanish actor is married to Penélope Cruz?
questions.fact: They first worked together on "Jamón, jamón" (1992), when she was still a teenager, and married in 2010.

questions.question: Which Spice Girl married footballer David Beckham?
questions.fact: The family lived in Madrid while David played for Real Madrid, from 2003 to 2007.

questions.question: Which singer retold Romeo and Juliet in her 2008 hit "Love Story"?
questions.fact: Her version has a happy ending: instead of the lovers dying, Romeo proposes and her father gives his blessing.

questions.question: In which country do women traditionally give men chocolate on Valentine's Day?
questions.fact: A month later, on 14 March ("White Day"), men are expected to return the favour, traditionally with white chocolate or sweets.

questions.question: Which brain chemical, linked to reward and craving, is highly active when you fall in love?
questions.fact: Brain scans by anthropologist Helen Fisher's team found new love lights up reward areas rich in dopamine, the same system involved in cravings.

questions.question: In the famous 1945 photo of a kiss in Times Square, what is the man dressed as?
questions.fact: Alfred Eisenstaedt took it for Life magazine on VJ Day. The woman, often called a nurse, was reportedly a dental assistant.

questions.question: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle married in 2018 in a chapel at which castle?
questions.fact: They married in St George's Chapel. Meghan had been an actress, best known for the US legal drama "Suits".

questions.question: In which Madrid church did Felipe VI and Letizia marry in 2004?
questions.fact: Before the wedding Letizia Ortiz was a well-known journalist and news presenter on Spanish public TV (TVE).

questions.question: Which British king gave up the throne in 1936 to marry Wallis Simpson?
questions.fact: Wallis was an American divorcee. After abdicating he became the Duke of Windsor, and they married in France in 1937.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife?
questions.fact: He spent his last years under house arrest, held by his own son Aurangzeb, reportedly with a view of the Taj from his window.

questions.question: In which Shakespeare comedy do Beatrice and Benedick trade witty insults before falling in love?
questions.fact: The play is set in Messina, Sicily, and the prince in it, Don Pedro, comes from Aragon in Spain.

questions.question: In "Romeo, Romeo, wherefore art thou Romeo?", what does "wherefore" mean?
questions.fact: Juliet isn't looking for him: she's asking why he has to be a Montague, the family her own family hates.

questions.question: Who wrote "Wuthering Heights", the stormy love story of Heathcliff and Cathy?
questions.fact: It was her only novel, published in 1847 under the male pen name Ellis Bell. She died the following year, aged 30.

questions.question: In Greek myth, whose face "launched a thousand ships"?
questions.fact: The famous line comes from Christopher Marlowe's play "Doctor Faustus", written around 1590, not from Homer.

questions.question: Who wrote and first recorded "I Will Always Love You", later a huge hit for Whitney Houston?
questions.fact: By her own account, Parton turned down Elvis Presley's offer to record it because his manager wanted half the publishing rights.

questions.question: Which Righteous Brothers song plays during the famous pottery scene in "Ghost"?
questions.fact: The song was written in 1955 for a little-known prison film called "Unchained", which is where its title comes from.

questions.question: Which film has the line "You had me at hello"?
questions.fact: Renée Zellweger says it to Tom Cruise. The same 1996 film gave us the catchphrase "Show me the money!".

questions.question: Mexican painter Frida Kahlo was married to which fellow artist?
questions.fact: They married twice: they divorced in 1939 and remarried in San Francisco in 1940.

questions.question: In 1969 John Lennon and Yoko Ono married in which territory next to Spain?
questions.fact: Their honeymoon was a week-long "bed-in" for peace at the Amsterdam Hilton, with the press invited into their hotel room.

questions.question: At a Spanish wedding, the groom traditionally gives the bride 13 coins called…
questions.fact: The coins are blessed during the ceremony and stand for prosperity and the couple's promise to share everything they own.

questions.question: What does the groom traditionally stamp on and break at the end of a Jewish wedding?
questions.fact: It is often said to recall the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem, and guests then shout "Mazel tov!" (congratulations).

questions.question: At Indian weddings, what are the intricate henna designs on the bride's hands called?
questions.fact: A popular saying goes that the darker the henna stain turns, the stronger the love between the couple will be.

questions.question: Which jewellery company's 1947 slogan was "A Diamond Is Forever"?
questions.fact: Copywriter Frances Gerety wrote it, and in 1999 Advertising Age named it the best advertising slogan of the 20th century.

questions.question: What is the traditional gift for a 40th wedding anniversary?
questions.fact: Pearl is for 30 years, sapphire 45 and emerald 55. Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip reached platinum (70 years) in 2017.

questions.question: What does the Portuguese word "saudade" describe?
options: The nerves of a first kiss
Longing for someone or something absent
questions.fact: It is at the heart of fado, Portugal's melancholy music, and is often called one of the hardest words to translate.

questions.question: What does the French phrase "coup de foudre" mean in love?
questions.fact: It literally means "a bolt of lightning". Spanish has a similar word, "flechazo", from "flecha" (arrow).

questions.question: Which Roman festival in mid-February is sometimes linked to the origins of Valentine's Day?
questions.fact: Pope Gelasius I is said to have suppressed it in the 490s, though historians still debate whether it's really connected to Valentine's Day.

questions.question: In which country is "Dia dos Namorados", the lovers' day, celebrated on 12 June?
questions.fact: The date is the eve of Saint Anthony's Day, and Saint Anthony is seen as a matchmaker saint in Brazil and Portugal.

questions.question: Which Paris bridge had so many "love locks" that its railing panels were removed in 2015?
questions.fact: The locks were estimated to weigh about 45 tonnes, and part of a railing collapsed under their weight in 2014.

questions.question: The wedding ring finger was once thought to contain the "vein of love". What was it called in Latin?
questions.fact: The idea is a myth: every finger has similar veins, and none runs directly to the heart.

questions.question: In Spanish, "novio" can mean boyfriend or…
questions.fact: Likewise "novia" means both girlfriend and bride, so only the context tells you if someone is dating or getting married.

questions.question: Which English poet is often credited with the earliest known link between Valentine's Day and romance?
questions.fact: His poem "Parlement of Foules", written around 1380, describes birds choosing their mates "on Seynt Valentynes day".

questions.question: One theory says the heart symbol comes from the seed pod of which ancient plant?
questions.fact: Silphium grew around Cyrene, in modern Libya. It was so valuable it appeared on coins, and it is thought to have been harvested to extinction.

questions.question: What is Mr Darcy's first name in "Pride and Prejudice"?
questions.fact: Colin Firth's famous wet-shirt lake scene in the 1995 BBC adaptation does not appear in Jane Austen's novel at all.

questions.question: Who is often credited with giving the first recorded diamond engagement ring, in 1477?
questions.fact: He gave it to Mary of Burgundy. Their grandson became Charles I of Spain, also known as Holy Roman Emperor Charles V.

questions.question: In Wales, which saint's day on 25 January is celebrated as a day for lovers?
questions.fact: Welsh men traditionally carved wooden "love spoons" as gifts to show their feelings and their skill.

questions.question: Rodin's sculpture "The Kiss" shows a couple from which poet's work?
questions.fact: The lovers are Paolo and Francesca from Dante's "Inferno". Look closely: their lips don't actually touch.

questions.question: "Broken heart syndrome", a real heart condition triggered by stress, is also called…
questions.fact: "Takotsubo" means "octopus pot" in Japanese, because the stunned heart balloons into a similar shape. Most people recover fully.
